rows.q: What is our replenishment policy for high-risk inventory?
rows.message: This is a SAMPLE policy written for the DSports AI proof of concept. The planning target is a 95% cycle service level. Safety stock covers demand uncertainty over the supplier lead time and is calculated from forecast error. The reorder point is the forecast demand over the lead time plus the safety stock. Stock is reviewed weekly. The recommended quantity brings the inventory position up to the forecast demand over the lead time and review period plus the safety stock, rounded up to the supplier's case pack and raised to the minimum order quantity.

rows.q: What is the minimum order quantity for our suppliers?
rows.message: This is a SAMPLE document written for the DSports AI proof of concept. For products priced below ₹5,000, the Minimum Order Quantity (MOQ) is 6, 12, 24, or 48 units, and they ship in case packs of 6. For bats, bicycles, and premium shoes, the MOQ is 2, 4, or 6 units with no case pack. The replenishment recommendation always rounds up to the exact MOQ and case pack held in the inventory master data. A purchase order quantity is raised to the MOQ even if the calculated need is smaller, and then rounded up to a whole number of case packs. If an open purchase order will arrive after the projected stock-out date, the buyer asks the supplier to expedite it before raising a new order. (Source: Supplier Lead Times and MOQ).

rows.q: What is the clearance policy for inventory older than 90 days?
rows.message: This is a SAMPLE policy written for the DSports AI proof of concept. Inventory older than 90 days is reviewed monthly for clearance. Stock older than 120 days with at least 150 days of cover is critical aging and reviewed first. A clearance discount of up to 50% can be proposed by merchandising, but discounts above 50% need approval from the Head of Merchandising and the Finance controller. No promotion may leave a unit margin below 10% of the discounted selling price. Standard clearance promotions run for 14 days.

rows.q: Who needs to approve a discount above 50%?
rows.message:
This is a SAMPLE policy written for the DSports AI proof of concept; it is not DSports' real pricing policy.
Inventory older than 90 days is reviewed for clearance every month. Inventory with more than 120 days of cover is classed as slow moving; with at least 180 days of cover it is high overstock. Stock older than 120 days that also has at least 150 days of cover is critical aging and is reviewed first. A clearance discount of up to 50% can be proposed by the merchandising team without further approval. A discount above 50% needs approval from the Head of Merchandising and the Finance controller. No promotion may leave a unit margin below 10% of the discounted selling price. Standard clearance promotions run for 14 days and are reviewed before they are extended. Do not start a clearance on a sport while one of its major events is in its demand window; stock is held for the event. The DSports pricing and promotion engine is the only system that changes prices. The AI recommends a scenario; a business user must approve it and the pricing engine applies it, with an audit record. The AI assistant never changes a price and never launches a promotion.

rows.q: Which of those is better?
rows.message:
This is POC synthetic data. No single discount for all 3 products keeps every product above the 10% margin floor; 30% and 50% discounts break it for at least one product. Discounting only 1 of the 3 products at its individual best discount gives a net benefit of ₹815.

A 30% discount could sell 116.7 units, generating ₹165,541 revenue and ₹21,851 margin, reducing inventory by 54.9 units valued at ₹65,181. A 50% discount could sell 215.8 units, generating ₹209,544 revenue but a negative margin of ₹-48,452, reducing inventory by 154.0 units valued at ₹179,662.
